samples.summary: Scope creep past the issue's stated "no new behavior": API-key authority semantics are rewritten across the entire v1 surface, not just the new folder/copy routes
samples.evidence: The todo (docs/tasks/active/20260903-api-v1-folders-copy-todo.md:82-85) says "Out of scope … Nothing here is a new capability: every endpoint's behavior already ships, only the way to call it without a browser is new", and the note added to agentic-office-workflow.md summarizes A′ as "An `/api/v1` surface **and** a CLI command — no new behavior". The diff nonetheless changes behavior of already-shipped endpoints for existing keys: `WorkspaceScopeGuard` now runs `assertMember(resolvedId, user.id)` for API keys (previously scope match alone returned true); `ApiV1DocumentsController.remove` now applies the `isDocumentManager` bar to API keys that were previously waved through with workspace authority (documents.controller.ts:175-184, and backend.md's "act with workspace authority" paragraph had to be rewritten); `ApiV1ImageReadController.assertCanRead` now requires the minter's live membership; and `WorkspaceService.removeMember` now revokes keys in a transaction. Impact outside the codebase: a key whose minter was demoted or whose workspace ownership was transferred silently loses delete/move and even image reads — an integration-breaking change bundled into a surface-parity PR, and arguably brushing rest-api.md's "Granular per-document … permission scoping on API keys" non-goal (rest-api.md:34).

samples.summary: `document-copy.md` still lists "REST v1 / CLI copy — not exposed there; the web list is the only caller" as a Non-Goal, which this change makes false, and that canonical doc is not updated
samples.evidence: The diff adds `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/documents/:did/copy` and `wafflebase docs copy`, and records the reversal in rest-api.md §5.1 and agentic-office-workflow.md §3.1 — but document-copy.md, the doc the new controller comment points readers at (documents.controller.ts:88), still declares the surface a Non-Goal. workspace-folders.md got exactly the "Also delivered" note this doc is missing, so the pattern for fixing it is established in this same diff.

samples.summary: Folder authorization/branching logic is copied from `FolderController` rather than shared, so the web and v1 folder permission rules can now diverge
samples.evidence: `ApiV1FoldersController.update`/`remove` reproduce `FolderController.update`/`remove` (folder.controller.ts:74-119) line for line: the same `assertMember` + `isDocumentManager` helper (`resolveFolderManager` vs `isManager`), the same `name`/`parentId` split, the same `assertSameWorkspace` → `assertNoCycle` ordering, and the same two error strings. Only `FolderService` is shared. A future change to the manager rule or the cycle-check ordering must be made twice or the two surfaces will answer differently for the same folder. (The repo does keep parallel v1 controllers elsewhere, so this is consistent with existing shape — hence minor — but the gate logic itself is duplicated, not just the routing.)

samples.summary: The v1 document `PATCH` hand-rolls an inline body type and manual field copying instead of reusing the existing validated `UpdateDocumentDto`
samples.evidence: `UpdateDocumentDto` (document/document.dto.ts:92-106) already models exactly this body — `@Length(1,200) title?`, `@IsUUID() folderId?: string | null` with the documented "undefined = unchanged, null = root" contract added by workspace-folders.md. The v1 handler instead takes `@Body() body: { title?: string; folderId?: string | null }`, which the new spec itself notes means `ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true })` strips nothing, so the surface accepts an over-long title and a non-UUID `folderId` where the web path rejects both. Reusing (or subclassing minus `workspaceId`) the DTO would give whitelisting and validation for free and keep one definition of the move contract — the folders controller in this same diff does reuse `CreateFolderDto`/`UpdateFolderDto`.

samples.summary: Folder navigation is only half-reachable from v1: documents can be filed into folders but the document list has no `?folderId=` filter and `POST /documents` cannot create into a folder, unlike the web surface
samples.evidence: workspace-folders.md:151-153 specifies `GET workspaces/:wid/documents?folderId=` (omitted = root) and `CreateDocumentInWorkspaceDto.folderId` for the web surface; the v1 list (`ApiV1DocumentsController.list`, documents.controller.ts:40-52) still returns every document in the workspace with no folder filter, and `create` (line 54-72) ignores `folderId`. Neither is one of the seven A′ items, and full `Document` rows do carry `folderId` so a client can filter locally — so the stated acceptance is met — but an agent's folder workflow is asymmetric with the browser's.

finding.summary: Scope creep past the issue's stated "no new behavior": API-key authority semantics are rewritten across the entire v1 surface, not just the new folder/copy routes
finding.evidence: The todo (docs/tasks/active/20260903-api-v1-folders-copy-todo.md:82-85) says "Out of scope … Nothing here is a new capability: every endpoint's behavior already ships, only the way to call it without a browser is new", and the note added to agentic-office-workflow.md summarizes A′ as "An `/api/v1` surface **and** a CLI command — no new behavior". The diff nonetheless changes behavior of already-shipped endpoints for existing keys: `WorkspaceScopeGuard` now runs `assertMember(resolvedId, user.id)` for API keys (previously scope match alone returned true); `ApiV1DocumentsController.remove` now applies the `isDocumentManager` bar to API keys that were previously waved through with workspace authority (documents.controller.ts:175-184, and backend.md's "act with workspace authority" paragraph had to be rewritten); `ApiV1ImageReadController.assertCanRead` now requires the minter's live membership; and `WorkspaceService.removeMember` now revokes keys in a transaction. Impact outside the codebase: a key whose minter was demoted or whose workspace ownership was transferred silently loses delete/move and even image reads — an integration-breaking change bundled into a surface-parity PR, and arguably brushing rest-api.md's "Granular per-document … permission scoping on API keys" non-goal (rest-api.md:34).

verdict.reason: The code exists as described (WorkspaceScopeGuard:44 asserts the minter's live membership for API keys; documents.controller.ts:175-184 applies isDocumentManager to every caller; image-read.controller.ts:97-112 repeats the pair; workspace.service.ts:115-124 revokes keys transactionally), but it is not blocking under the design-fit rubric. (a) No acceptance criterion is unmet — every planned route/command lands. (b) The alleged spec breach misreads its citation: todo:84-85 says "Nothing here is a new **capability**", a statement about which features exist, while the SAME todo's Plan at lines 49-53 explicitly specifies this authority model ("An API key is **not** waved past it — it carries the authority of `ApiKey.createdBy`, resolved against that user's membership at request time"), and the Decision at 24-37 makes WorkspaceScopeGuard the load-bearing element of the close. So the semantics are in-spec, not creep. (c) The cited Non-Goal (rest-api.md:34) is "Granular **per-document or per-cell** permission scoping on API keys" — this change is workspace-level membership liveness, the opposite granularity direction, so no stated Non-Goal is crossed. (d) The claimed external cost is overstated: assertMember passes for a demoted (member-role) minter, so demotion costs neither reads nor image reads; only a removed minter is refused, and removeMember now revokes those keys by design, and keys minted by a live owner (the only minters, per assertOwner) are unaffected. (e) Design-doc discipline is satisfied — the semantics are folded into the canonical docs (rest-api.md:504-535, backend.md:291-299, agentic-office-workflow.md:195-202), not a parallel doc. What is left is a documented hardening generalized one guard wider than strictly needed: a real fit point whose cost stays inside the codebase's own coherence, i.e. minor, which never blocks.
